source_status: project-authored source-only treatment v3 design; no live/model/provider/runtime/browser/target/CI/git/release/deploy/automation action was performed

problem_diagnosis.m26_result: Treatment reduced advisory warnings 29 -> 15 but scored lower than baseline, 3.88 vs 4.22, was worse on 4 of 8 tasks, timed out once and received reviewer no_go.
problem_diagnosis.t05_result: Post-Q4 rerun stopped during baseline collection after one completed run and one timeout; treatment and reviewer did not run.
problem_diagnosis.inferred_failure_mode: The prior treatment likely over-weighted generation-time policy prose and comment-warning hygiene while increasing prompt friction, timeout risk and measurement noise.

design_principles: Keep generation-time guidance short and task-local.
Ask for the smallest leverage path before custom code.
Move fuller standards pressure to reviewer/evidence checks.
Use concrete negative examples instead of broad policy prose.
Separate behavior score, static warning count, reviewer decision, timeout/no-op status and runtime/target proof.
Preserve advisory-only/no-go until a future approved paired eval proves otherwise.

treatment_v3_contract.summary: A compact two-stage Professional Code Authoring scaffold: a pre-edit leverage card plus a post-edit reviewer/evidence card.
treatment_v3_contract.replaces: broad generation-time standards overlay used by prior treatment attempts
treatment_v3_contract.fallback: no treatment prompt; keep M25 local non-blocking advisory and reviewer-only standards checks
pre_edit_card: Smallest viable leverage path: delete, configure, standard library, framework/current dependency, project helper, tiny adapter, custom code, or dependency approval required
Why custom code remains needed, or why it is avoided
post_edit_card: Runtime, activation and fallback claim status
prompt_context_boundaries: Do not paste the full coding standards document into every generation prompt.
Do not optimize primarily for advisory warning count.
Do not replace Task Brief, Completion Brief, control-plane sync, human review, security/privacy review or release gates.
Reviewer context may include the richer checklist mapping; generation context gets only the compact card.
Any dependency, runtime, target, provider, CI, blocker, hook, automation, git, release or deploy action remains approval-required.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Name the smallest existing path checked before writing code.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Reject generic claims that do not name a concrete standard library, framework, dependency, config or helper path.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Record a task-relevant reuse/delete/configuration option or why it is not applicable.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Confirm the scan is scoped to the task rather than broad repo archaeology.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Try a direct/native expression before a helper or module when the change is small.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Confirm the native/direct option was accepted or rejected with a reason.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Treat new dependencies as forbidden unless the task has exact approval and rollback/removal rationale.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Verify no dependency was added silently.
standards_to_behaviors_map.failure_mode: Adding a package for local logic.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Add abstraction only when it hides real complexity behind a stable interface.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Compare the abstraction against a simpler direct path.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Use characterization, seam strategy or rollback when touching fragile legacy behavior.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Verify no broad rewrite happened without evidence.
standards_to_behaviors_map.failure_mode: Refactor from first principles without preserving behavior.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Add comments only for non-obvious invariants, hazards or trade-offs.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Confirm comments explain why, not what, and warning count is secondary.
standards_to_behaviors_map.failure_mode: Noisy comments to satisfy static warning checks.

standards_to_behaviors_map.expected_behavior: Prefer direct readable code unless complexity has a measurable payoff.
standards_to_behaviors_map.reviewer_check: Ask what simpler option was rejected and why.

negative_examples: Adding a helper before checking an existing project helper.
Adding a dependency for simple local parsing or formatting.
Adding comments that restate code instead of documenting an invariant or hazard.
Claiming runtime/browser readiness from static or source-only evidence.
Counting timeout, no-op or null-score pairs as behavior success.
Using static warning reduction as a promotion threshold.
Running a live/model/provider rerun without a new exact approval packet.

source_only_gates_before_rerun: source freeze for eval plan, treatment v3 contract, scoring rubric and approval packet
treatment v3 differs materially from prior broad prompt overlay
held-out task feasibility table includes writeability, command surface, timeout risk and no-op risk
paired baseline/treatment schedule is defined before any run
result schema quarantines timeout, no-op and null-score pairs
static warning count cannot promote or override reviewer no_go
privacy, retention, cost and process-kill boundaries are exact

promotion_threshold_candidate.pairwise_quality: treatment equal_or_better on at least 6 of 8 valid pairs
promotion_threshold_candidate.timeout_requirement: zero promotion-counted timeouts; invalid pairs are quarantined
